tasks.title: pipeline/crypto.py: Fernet vault with key rotation, fail-closed key handling
tasks.notes: Research docs/_research/2026-09-21_management-ui.md section 7 (key management table). Pure module: it must NOT import pipeline.health or pipeline.connections (import cycles later). Define SecretKeyMissing(RuntimeError), SecretKeyInvalid(RuntimeError), SecretDecryptError(RuntimeError). class Vault: Vault(keys: list[str]) builds a cryptography MultiFernet (first key is primary); Vault.from_env_value(value: Optional[str]) -> Optional[Vault] splits on commas, strips, ignores blanks and returns None when no key is present (the caller decides what None means); a malformed key raises SecretKeyInvalid naming the key POSITION only, never the key text. Methods: encrypt(text)->str, decrypt(token)->str (raises SecretDecryptError with a generic message; never echoes ciphertext, plaintext or keys), encrypt_json(dict)->str and decrypt_json(token)->dict (envelope for a secrets dict, unicode safe), rotate(token)->str (re-encrypt under the primary), and module function generate_key()->str. CLI: python -m pipeline.crypto genkey prints a fresh key on one line followed by a second line reminding the operator to keep it in .env, back it up separately from data/, and that losing it loses every stored secret. Never log or print keys anywhere except genkey. Do not pass a ttl to decrypt (secrets are long lived). Tests: round trip; wrong key -> SecretDecryptError; rotation (token from the old key decrypts with a [new, old] vault, after rotate the old key alone fails and the new works); blank, whitespace and comma-only values -> None; malformed key -> SecretKeyInvalid with no key text in str(exc); encrypt_json unicode round trip; no plaintext or ciphertext in any exception message; genkey CLI output is a valid Fernet key (run it via subprocess with the venv python).

tasks.title: pipeline/redact.py: one redaction function for persisted and returned text
tasks.notes: Research docs/_research/2026-09-21_management-ui.md section 2 (leak surface): HealthResult.detail, CollectionResult.detail, Run.error and Run.summary carry str(exc) and upstream error bodies into the DB and /api/status. Implement redact(text: object, secrets: Iterable[str] = (), *, max_len: Optional[int] = None) -> str. Never raises: non-str input is converted with str(). Replaces every supplied secret value of length >= 6 (longest first; also its URL-encoded and JSON-escaped forms) and every known token shape with the literal [redacted]: Slack tokens xox[abprs]-..., Authorization values (Bearer and Basic), key=value or JSON pairs for refresh_token, access_token, client_secret, code, code_verifier, password, Google ya29. access tokens, 1// refresh tokens and GOCSPX- client secrets, Anthropic sk-ant- keys, and JWT-shaped strings (eyJ....). Truncates to max_len AFTER redaction when given. Patterns compiled once and linear-time safe: no nested quantifiers; a test feeds 200000-character adversarial inputs and asserts completion well under a second. Idempotent (redacting twice equals once). Must not mangle ordinary text: ISO dates, email addresses, UUIDs, short words. Tests: each pattern; supplied secret in plain, URL-encoded and JSON-escaped form; short secrets (under 6) ignored; overlapping secrets; non-str input; the adversarial timing; idempotence; the not-mangled set.

tasks.title: pipeline/connections.py: validated CRUD with write-only views
tasks.notes: Contracts are in plan.md (Contracts section) and research docs/_research/2026-09-21_management-ui.md Decisions. The module must NOT import pipeline.config_store and must not import pipeline.health at module level. KINDS spec: m365 {config: alias(label), tenant_id, client_id; secrets: none}; zoom {config: account_id, client_id; secrets: client_secret; singleton with label zoom}; slack {config: label; secrets: token}; gmail {config: label, client_id, redirect_mode (paste_back|callback, default paste_back); secrets: client_secret, refresh_token (optional at create: sign-in sets it)}. Validation (raise ConnectionError subclasses that carry a FIELD NAME and a message that NEVER contains a submitted value): slack and gmail labels ^[a-z0-9]+$ max 32; m365 alias ^[A-Za-z0-9-]+$ max 40 (it becomes a token file name, so no path characters); id is derived (m365_<alias>, zoom, slack_<label>, gmail_<label>); ids and identifiers non-empty with a sane charset and length; secret values non-empty strings; unknown kinds and unknown fields rejected. Vault: set_vault(vault) and get_vault() module state (loaded elsewhere); a write that includes secrets and has no vault raises SecretKeyMissing (from pipeline.crypto). API: create(kind, fields) -> ConnectionView; update(id, config=None, secrets=None) replaces only the secret names provided and leaves others untouched; delete(id) writes a Tombstone, removes the row and returns bool; get(id); list_connections(); exists(id); set_secret(id, name, value) (used by sign-in). ConnectionView is a plain dataclass with id, kind, label, origin, config, secrets_set (sorted NAMES of secrets that have a value), created_at, updated_at and NEVER a secret value or ciphertext. Creating an id that has a live row raises DuplicateConnection; creating a tombstoned id clears its tombstone. Every write bumps a module-level version counter exposed by current_version(). A module-private _secrets_for(id) -> dict returns decrypted secrets for the materialize task only. Tests (temp_db plus a Vault from crypto.generate_key()): each kind's create, update and delete; the validation matrix including traversal aliases (../x, a/b, a b), uppercase labels rejected for slack and gmail, zoom singleton; the write-only property (json.dumps of every view contains no secret value and no ciphertext); update replaces only named secrets; delete tombstones; no vault plus secrets raises SecretKeyMissing; error messages never contain a submitted secret.

tasks.title: Connections: seed from env once, materialize env-style keys, secret values, overlay provider
tasks.notes: Research docs/_research/2026-09-21_management-ui.md section 1 (corrections 1-4, 6). Continue in pipeline/connections.py. (1) seed_from_env(raw_env: Mapping[str,str]) -> list[str]: for every connection the RAW env declares (M365: each M365_ORG<n>_ALIAS with its TENANT_ID and a client id of M365_ORG<n>_CLIENT_ID else the shared M365_CLIENT_ID; zoom when ZOOM_ACCOUNT_ID, ZOOM_CLIENT_ID and ZOOM_CLIENT_SECRET are all present; SLACK_<LABEL>_TOKEN; GMAIL_<LABEL>_REFRESH_TOKEN with client id and secret from GMAIL_<LABEL>_CLIENT_ID and GMAIL_<LABEL>_CLIENT_SECRET else the shared GMAIL_CLIENT_ID and GMAIL_CLIENT_SECRET), create it with origin env ONLY IF its id has no live row AND no tombstone; return the seeded ids; idempotent; a malformed declaration (for example a missing tenant id) is skipped and reported, never raises; with no vault it seeds nothing and returns []. Existing rows are never overwritten from .env (STORE WINS). (2) materialize() -> dict[str,str]: the env-style overlay for live rows using EXACTLY the key families health.py already parses: slack -> SLACK_<LABEL upper>_TOKEN; gmail -> GMAIL_<LABEL>_REFRESH_TOKEN (only when set) plus per-label GMAIL_<LABEL>_CLIENT_ID and GMAIL_<LABEL>_CLIENT_SECRET; m365 -> M365_ORG<n>_ALIAS, _TENANT_ID and _CLIENT_ID with n numbered 1..N by row seq then created_at; zoom -> ZOOM_ACCOUNT_ID, ZOOM_CLIENT_ID, ZOOM_CLIENT_SECRET. (3) is_family_key(name) -> bool and FAMILY_KEY_PATTERNS: compiled regexes for every connection-owned key family (M365_ORG<n>_*, M365_CLIENT_ID, SLACK_<L>_TOKEN, ZOOM_ACCOUNT_ID, ZOOM_CLIENT_ID, ZOOM_CLIENT_SECRET, GMAIL_CLIENT_ID, GMAIL_CLIENT_SECRET, GMAIL_<L>_REFRESH_TOKEN, GMAIL_<L>_CLIENT_ID, GMAIL_<L>_CLIENT_SECRET) but NOT SLACK_SKIP_DMS, TZ, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, SIGNALSLATE_MAP_MODEL or any other non-connection key. (4) secret_values() -> list[str]: every decrypted non-empty secret in the store, for redact(). (5) overlay_provider() -> Optional[dict]: returns a cached immutable dict rebuilt only when current_version() changed (thread-safe swap under a lock) and returns None when no vault is configured, so the caller keeps pure .env behavior. Prove round trip: with health._env monkeypatched to return the materialized dict, the EXISTING health functions m365_aliases, m365_tenant_config, slack_workspaces and gmail_accounts must return the seeded values unchanged. Tests: seed matrix (each kind, shared vs per-org client id, tombstoned id not re-seeded, idempotent second call, malformed skipped, no vault seeds nothing, existing row not overwritten); materialize per kind including M365 numbering stability across delete and re-add; family-key classification including the NOT-family keys above; cache invalidation on a write; the health round trip; secret_values excludes empties. ADDED at build time (from T-006 review): also add a narrow PUBLIC accessor get_secret(connection_id, name) -> Optional[str] returning one decrypted secret (None when absent), documented as for the token-exchange and sign-in flows only: callers must never log or return the value. T-016 needs the Gmail client_secret and T-017 reads nothing secret; do not widen _secrets_for. Test that it returns the stored value, None for a missing name or id, and raises SecretDecryptError-safe generic errors without echoing ciphertext.

tasks.title: pipeline/tokencache.py: per-alias lock, atomic 0600 writes, corrupt-file tolerance
tasks.notes: Codebase finding Q3: the MSAL cache read-modify-write has no lock and writes with write_text (truncate then write, default umask), and a truncated file makes deserialize raise out of check_all_configured and fails the whole run. New module: cache_path(alias) -> Path (TOKEN_DIR defaults to the repo tokens/ directory and is monkeypatchable; validates alias against ^[A-Za-z0-9-]+$ and raises ValueError otherwise: path traversal guard), alias_lock(alias) -> threading.Lock (one lock per alias, created under a module lock), load(alias) -> Optional[msal.SerializableTokenCache] (None when the file is absent; a corrupt or truncated file also returns None and never raises), save(alias, cache) -> None (only when cache.has_state_changed; atomic: write a temp file in the same directory with mode 0600 then os.replace; mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)), and a context manager locked(alias) that holds the alias lock around a load-modify-save sequence. Stdlib plus msal only. Tests: path validation (traversal, separators, empty); atomic replace (make os.replace raise between write and replace: the old file stays intact); file mode 0600; corrupt file -> None; absent -> None; save skipped when state unchanged; two threads on the same alias serialize while different aliases do not block each other.

tasks.title: Runner: single-source runs, atomic run guard, per-run snapshot, last-attempt recording, config toggles
tasks.notes: Research docs/_research/2026-09-21_management-ui.md section 3 and codebase findings Q4 and Q6. (1) execute_run(trigger='manual', only: Optional[str]=None): when only is given, validate it is in known_sources() (ValueError before any Run row is written), run the health check and collection for that source only (check_all_configured({only: True}) and the existing _active filter) while still creating the Run row, SourceHealth rows and using the same per-source cursor, backfill and failure-streak logic; Run.trigger for such runs is manual-source (do NOT edit db.py: mention it in the docstring; the web type is extended in the API and web tasks). (2) Close the check-then-insert race: a module-level threading.Lock around has_running_run() plus the Run insert so the scheduler and UI triggers cannot both start; the loser still raises RunAlreadyInProgress (contract unchanged). (3) Wrap the body of the run in health.env_snapshot() so one run sees one consistent config even if the store changes mid-run. (4) After each source's collection call db.record_attempt(source, result.status, result.detail, persisted_count); also for a raised exception (status error, detail = the exception CLASS NAME only). Do not change any status, cursor or streak logic. (5) config_store.py: add forget_source(source_id) (remove the id from the stored active_sources under the module _lock and write the file) and set_source_active(source_id, active: bool) (load merged, set, save). Neither may call into pipeline.connections (deadlock hazard: load_config holds _lock while known_sources() runs). tests/test_runner.py must pass unchanged. Tests: only=X collects only X and leaves other sources' cursors untouched; unknown only raises ValueError and writes no Run; the lock: two concurrent execute_run calls yield exactly one Run row and one RunAlreadyInProgress; snapshot: a store change injected between the health and collect phases is not observed inside the run; record_attempt written for ok, partial, error and raised-exception cases; forget_source and set_source_active round trip and a deleted id's old toggle does not resurrect on re-create.

tasks.title: pipeline/oauth_flows.py: pending-flow store, nonce binding, paste-back URL validation
tasks.notes: Research docs/_research/2026-09-21_management-ui.md section 6 (every rule). Provider-agnostic pure logic with an in-process store (single uvicorn process; pending flows do not survive a restart: document it). PendingFlow dataclass: flow_id, provider, connection_id, mode (paste_back|callback), state, redirect_uri, payload (provider flow dict including code_verifier: NEVER returned to a browser), nonce_hash, created_at, expires_at. FlowStore with a lock: create(provider, connection_id, mode, state, redirect_uri, payload, ttl_seconds=900, now=None) -> (PendingFlow, nonce) where nonce = secrets.token_urlsafe(32) and only its sha256 is stored; consume(state=None, flow_id=None, nonce=None, provider=None, now=None) -> PendingFlow atomically removes the record and raises FlowError subclasses (UnknownFlow, ExpiredFlow, NonceMismatch, ProviderMismatch) with generic messages; comparisons via hmac.compare_digest; a wrong nonce must NOT consume the record (so an attacker cannot burn a victim's flow; document and test); expired records are purged on every call; at most 20 pending flows (oldest evicted). parse_pasted_url(url, *, allowed_hosts=('127.0.0.1','localhost')) -> dict returns only {code, state, error, error_description} (each str capped at 2 KB): reject length over 4096, a non-http scheme, a host that is not exactly in allowed_hosts (case-insensitive), userinfo, a missing query; NEVER fetch the URL; a fragment-only response (code after #) raises a specific FlowError telling the user to use query mode; no exception message ever contains the code or the full URL. build_callback_url(public_base_url, provider) -> f'{base}/api/oauth/callback/{provider}' (https only; provider in google or microsoft). Tests: TTL with an injected clock; single use; nonce binding; provider mismatch; eviction cap; purge; parse_pasted_url matrix (good loopback with a port, localhost, https rejected, other host rejected, the userinfo trick http://127.0.0.1@evil.example/, http://evil.example/?x=http://127.0.0.1, oversize, fragment-only, missing state, an error response); and a property test that FlowError messages never include the code.

tasks.title: pipeline/oauth_gmail.py: start and finish Google sign-in (paste-back and callback)
tasks.notes: Research docs/_research/2026-09-21_management-ui.md sections 4 and 6. start(connection_id, mode, *, store, public_base_url=None) -> StartResult(flow_id, auth_url, mode, expires_at, nonce, instructions): loads the gmail connection (client_id and client_secret via pipeline.connections; a clear error when either is missing), builds PKCE and state through pipeline.oauth_google, redirect_uri = for paste_back http://127.0.0.1:<port> with a fixed documented port constant (default 8765: nothing listens; a Desktop client accepts any loopback port) and for callback build_callback_url(public_base_url,'google') (an error when public_base_url is None: callback needs https); auth URL from oauth_google.build_auth_url (scope gmail.readonly ONLY, access_type=offline, prompt=consent, S256); the PendingFlow stores the code_verifier server-side. finish(flow, code, ...) -> ConnectionView: exchanges the code with the STORED redirect_uri and verifier via oauth_google.exchange_code, runs assert_granted (refresh token present and gmail.readonly granted, else a clear error), then connections.set_secret(connection_id, 'refresh_token', token) and returns the updated view (no secrets). finish_paste(store, flow_id, pasted_url, nonce) and finish_callback(store, state, code, nonce) wrap parse or consume plus finish. Errors map to typed exceptions with user-safe messages (denied consent, state problems, expired flow, exchange rejected with the status only). Never log or return the code, verifier, refresh token or client secret. Tests (network stubbed at requests.post inside pipeline.oauth_google): paste_back and callback happy paths store the refresh token ENCRYPTED (decrypt through the connections internals in the test); scope missing refused; no refresh token refused; callback without public_base_url refused; denied consent (error=access_denied); replay of the same state fails; expired flow; the exchange uses the STORED redirect_uri not a pasted one (assert the request body); the token and secrets never appear in any exception string or returned dict.

tasks.title: pipeline/oauth_m365.py: start and finish Microsoft sign-in with the MSAL two-step flow

tasks.notes: Research docs/_research/2026-09-21_management-ui.md sections 8 and 9 (verified by experiment): with today's wildcard CORS a custom header defense is void, strict CORS alone does not stop a simple POST (the handler still runs), body-less POSTs are the exposed ones, and the default 422 handler ECHOES submitted secrets in the input field. api/security.py: install_security(app, *, allowed_origins: list[str]) adds (a) CORSMiddleware with the explicit origin list, methods GET, POST, PATCH, PUT, DELETE and OPTIONS, allow_headers Content-Type and X-Requested-With, allow_credentials False; (b) a middleware that for every non-safe method (POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE) answers 403 unless the header X-Requested-With equals signalslate and, when an Origin header is present, it is in allowed_origins by exact match (GET and OPTIONS and the health route are exempt; the OAuth callback is a GET); requests that carry a body must have Content-Type application/json else 415; (c) a RequestValidationError handler returning 422 with per-error {type, loc, msg} ONLY (drop input, ctx and url) and NEVER using exc.body anywhere. hide_input_in_errors does not help under FastAPI. api/main.py: replace the wildcard CORS with install_security(app, allowed_origins=health.web_origins()); change nothing else. tasks.title: api/routers/oauth.py: start, paste-back finish and the real HTTPS callback
tasks.notes: Research docs/_research/2026-09-21_management-ui.md section 6. POST /oauth/{provider}/start {connection_id, mode} (provider google or microsoft; the connection kind must match: gmail with google, m365 with microsoft, else 400) -> {flow_id, auth_url, mode, expires_at, instructions}; the response sets an HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax cookie named ss_oauth_<flow_id> whose value is the nonce (Path=/api/oauth, Secure only when public_base_url is https, Max-Age = ttl); POST /oauth/{provider}/paste {flow_id, url} reads the nonce cookie, calls the provider finish_paste and returns {status: connected, connection: view}; GET /oauth/callback/{provider}?state=&code=&error= is unauthenticated by necessity: it validates state plus the nonce cookie through FlowStore.consume, calls finish_callback, then answers 302 to a FIXED target (the first allowed web origin plus /connections?oauth=ok, or ?oauth=error&reason=<code> where the reason is one of a small fixed set and never text from the provider or the query), always deletes the cookie, and never logs or echoes the code or state; an unknown or mismatched provider path gets the same generic error redirect. mode callback is refused with a clear 400 when health.public_base_url() is None.
